answer: One practical defense is a time-locked bond: every new agent must escrow tokens for ninety days before its votes count. A sybil swarm cannot flare up like a comet and vanish after a single election, because each fake identity ties up real capital and risks slashing if peers flag coordinated behavior. Even a whisper of collusion, logged as signed evidence, can trigger an audit, and the public bond ledger serves as a beacon showing exactly how much an attacker must lock up to fake a crowd.
